kitDescription: Ludmilla: Winter Owner is a water-element machine-gun attacker whose whole kit rewards keeping the trigger held down. Every 60 landed shots she marks the boss with a short 3-second damage-taken debuff the whole team benefits from, lands a bonus hit worth 158% of her attack, and tops up 20 rounds of her 300-round belt so she spends less time reloading. Every 60 core hits she fires a second, smaller bonus hit. Whenever any Full Burst begins — hers or a teammate's — she gains critical rate for 10 seconds. Her own burst is purely a self-buff: a large attack increase for 10 seconds plus a much faster reload for 20 seconds, keeping her sustained fire rolling.

redAssertions: F1 'S1a emits a boss-held debuff': expects buffApply.durationShots === undefined, engine emits null for timed buffs — serialization convention, blind-test artifact (RECON_ERROR), no faithfulness signal

F2 'S1a rider is self-sourced only': teammatesIdentical over-strict — SSOT §6: skill hits generate the caster's flat burst-gauge value, so removing the 158.43% rider legitimately shifts team rotation timing; helm stayed byte-identical while liter/crown moved 0.03%/0.002% — the blind's byte-identity premise contradicts the gauge SSOT (RECON_ERROR)

F3 'S1b refill raises her damage': sign assertion at +0.001% is rotation-alignment coupling, not a dead line — the robust observables confirm the refill is live and additive: reloads-to-max 18 vs 26, shots 8652 vs 8639 (more shots with the refill proves add-not-set semantics, resolving the S6 caveat empirically); blind over-strict (RECON_ERROR)
F4 'S2a rider is self-sourced only': same gauge-coupling artifact as F2 (RECON_ERROR)
F5 'Burst ATK durationShots': same null-vs-undefined convention as F1 (RECON_ERROR)

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA: all 7 kit lines are FAITHFUL with kit-literal magnitudes, correct triggers (hitCount 60 / 63-proxy / fullBurstEnter / burstCast), correct target sets (boss debuff vs self), and correct asymmetric durations, and every block verifiably FIRES at the prose cadence over 180s. Convergence is mechanically RED on 5 of 29 S5 assertions, but all 5 classify as blind-test artifacts, not driver divergences: two are a null-vs-undefined event-shape convention, two rest on a byte-identical-teammates premise that contradicts SSOT §6 (skill hits generate burst gauge, so removing a rider legitimately perturbs team rotation — helm stayed byte-identical), and one is a 0.001% damage-sign assertion swamped by rotation-alignment coupling whose robust observables (reloads 18 vs 26, shots 8652 vs 8639) the driver pins directly. The one substantive blind divergence (S6's hitCount-200 for the core-hit rider) is spurious — it assumes a 0.30 core rate that contradicts the engine's own flat 0.95 MG model, while the driver's 63 + requiresCore is whole-picture consistent and documented with a measurement recipe; the S6 filename-level leak is ruled non-voiding precisely because this divergence proves the blind never saw the driver's encoding. Discrimination is strong: naive-60 vs 63, coreHitRate:0 silencing, FB-entry (11) vs own-cast (6), the 600f duration delta, and the rider inertness pins are all RED under their named counterfactuals, and the cross-family reviewer independently named the same traps. Nothing must change for GO. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: (a) every agent inherited the engine's unmeasured flat 0.95 MG core rate, so the 63-proxy is stable-but-unvalidated — one real core-fraction footage read settles it; (b) the F3 explanation (0.001% sign inversion as rotation-alignment noise) is driver-asserted — a seeded Monte Carlo spread or a second deterministic arm of the no-refill counterfactual would confirm it is alignment coupling and not a subtly mis-routed effect.
